extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys/agents and participants in USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) reciprocal disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including what a respondent must file to raise a genuine issue of material fact and the consequences of failing to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may order reciprocal discipline where a practitioner has been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State; the OED served a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' seeking imposition of identical discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: the OED Director serves a complaint requesting reciprocal discipline; the USPTO Director issues an Order giving the respondent time to respond; if no genuine issue of material fact is raised under § 11.24(d) the identical discipline may be imposed. Example: here the OED Complaint requested public reprimand based on an Iowa public reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation predicated on being publicly reprimanded (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) / § 11.804(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (described in the document as § 11.804(4)) can be predicated upon a practitioner's having been publicly reprimanded by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director treated the Iowa Supreme Court public reprimand as the predicate for the USPTO violation. Where a state public reprimand exists, reciprocal discipline under the cited rule is a proper basis for USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's obligation to file a timely response (40-day period)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director issued an Order giving Respondent 40 days to file a response 'containing all information that Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact' under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To contest imposition of identical discipline, a respondent must timely present evidence/information within the specified period (40 days in this matter) sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact as to any of the permissible grounds in § 11.24(d)(1)(i)-(iv). Failure to do so supports imposition of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds to avoid identical reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)(i)-(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may avoid imposition of identical discipline by establishing a genuine issue of material fact based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)(i)-(iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order references these specific enumerated grounds (the respondent was invited to raise issues under them). Although the specific subclauses are not reproduced on this page, the practical criterion is that the respondent must identify and support one of the statutory grounds to prevent reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failing to raise a genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent 'does not raise any issue of material fact' and 'does not contest the imposition of reciprocal discipline,' the Director may determine that 'there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)' and impose the identical discipline (here: public reprimand).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical effect: an explicit acknowledgement by the respondent that no genuine issue exists is treated as consent and supports entry of the discipline. Respondent's concessions in the response were relied upon to impose the public reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and form of Notice of Public Reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall make public the prescribed Notice in the Official Gazette, which describes the respondent, the predicate state discipline, the rule violated, factual summary, and statutory citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice must include sufficient factual background and citation to the ethical rule(s). The Director accepted the respondent's suggestion to include the full citation to the Iowa Rules of Professional Conduct but declined other suggested redactions because the information was already publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of underlying state-court findings as predicate facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO relies on the factual findings and ethical conclusions made by the state authority (here, the Iowa Supreme Court) to predicate the USPTO discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice summarizes the state court's findings (e.g., that respondent 'assisted...in proofreading the estate planning instruments contrary to Rules 32:1.8(c) and (k)' and 'failed to explain to Client the conflict') and treats those findings as the basis for USPTO action unless a genuine dispute is raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific ethical rules cited (Iowa R. Prof. Conduct Rule 32:8.4(a); Rules 32:1.8(c) and (k); Rules 32:1.3(a)(2) and (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Iowa Supreme Court found violations of: Rule 32:8.4(a) (assisting in wrongdoing), Rules 32:1.8(c) and (k) (transactions with clients/conflicts), and Rules 32:1.3(a)(2) and (b) (duty to explain conflicts/need for independent counsel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These represent the substantive professional-conduct standards that formed the basis of the state reprimand. The USPTO incorporated those findings into its Notice. Practitioners should understand these ethical duties: avoid assisting in conflicted transactions, disclose conflicts and implications, and advise independent counsel when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests to redact or alter public factual details
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may propose wording changes to the Notice (e.g., to protect identity of non-PTO lawyers or firm names), but the Director may refuse changes where the information is 'already publicly available' and the changes are 'unnecessary and irrelevant' for the Notice's purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: proposals to omit or redact information from a public disciplinary Notice will be evaluated against public availability and relevance; public availability supports refusal to redact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public access to disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room (link provided) and the Notice will be published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order instructs the OED Director to make the Notice publicly available and cites where decisions can be accessed, emphasizing transparency and public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of final decision — judicial petition under 35 U.S.C. § 32
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.57(a) and 35 U.S.C. § 32, review of the final decision by the USPTO Director may be had by a Petition filed with the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural remedy: a respondent seeking review of the USPTO's final decision may file a petition in the specified federal district court per the cited statutes/regulations.
